% ======================================================================
% M1. The question (no title bar: the question fills the frame)
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=Q1]
\vfill
\begin{center}
\begin{minipage}{0.94\textwidth}\centering
{\Large\KeyIdea{Does a stronger bidder in a merger auction\\ scare off its competitor, or draw in more competition?}\par}
\end{minipage}
\end{center}
\vspace{1.4em}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{6pt}
\item A competitor pays to check the books before it can bid
\item Preemptive bids: a first bidder opens high, so the competitor stays out
\item To the target, one more bidder beats the best negotiation
\end{itemize}
\vfill
\GrayLine{Fishman 1988 \,|\, Bulow and Klemperer 1996}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M2. The traditional answer
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=Q2]{The traditional answer: strength deters entry}
\framesubtitle{Strength cuts the gain from entry}
\hypertarget{main:refs}{}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{7pt}
\item The bidder already in, the \textbf{incumbent}, is ready to bid
\item The next bidder, the \textbf{challenger}, must first \textbf{prepare}: diligence, finance, approvals
\item A stronger incumbent raises the price a victorious challenger pays
\item So preparation pays less, and fewer challengers enter
\item \textbf{Entry} is a choice: costs decide who shows up
\end{itemize}
\vspace{4pt}\GrayLine{Fishman 1988; Hirshleifer and Png 1989 \,|\, Samuelson 1985; Levin and Smith 1994}
\TakeawayWithNav[\ExhibitReadingGapRoomy]{Strength deters: entry pays less, so fewer challengers come.}
\PlaceNav{\hyperlink{app:refs}{\beamergotobutton{References}}}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M3. The answer in one frame
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=Q3]{Competition creates competition}
\framesubtitle{The channel is information in the stock price}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{7pt}
\item An outside investor knows the challenger class and can fill one order slot
\item A stronger incumbent shifts a value gap to target shareholders
\item Sale proceeds then depend more on the challenger class
\item Trade pays, the price becomes informative, good news covers a high cost
\item Entry rises at the benchmark: $\reg{entry_r0}\to\reg{entry_r1_B}$
\end{itemize}
\Takeaway[\ExhibitReadingGapRoomy]{\KeyIdea{The channel is information.} Hold price information fixed, and a stronger incumbent does not raise entry.}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M4. The decision interval
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=F1]{The target is for sale, and its stock still trades}
\framesubtitle{The decision interval}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[
  box/.style={draw=black!55, rounded corners=3pt, line width=0.6pt, align=center,
    text width=3.9cm, minimum height=0.85cm, font={\footnotesize\hyphenpenalty=10000\relax}, inner sep=3pt},
  arr/.style={-{Stealth[length=5pt]}, line width=0.7pt, black!60}]
  \node[box] (a) {Sale is public; one bidder is already in};
  \node[box, right=0.8cm of a] (b) {Target stock still trades};
  \node[box, right=0.8cm of b, draw=cCost, line width=1.1pt] (c)
    {Second bidder decides: pay to prepare, or stay out};
  \draw[arr] (a) -- (b);
  \draw[arr] (b) -- (c);
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
\vspace{-6pt}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{3pt}
\item One bidder is ready: the \textbf{incumbent}
\item Incumbent type gives a public clue to strength. Incumbent value stays private \graycite{Gorbenko and Malenko 2014}
\item A second bidder is not ready: the \textbf{challenger}
\item To bid, the challenger must first \textbf{prepare}: due diligence, finance, approvals
\item That step costs money and time. The name for that step is \textbf{entry}
\end{itemize}
\Takeaway[0.5em]{The focus is that interval: after the sale turns public, before the challenger decision.}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M5. The auction, the values and the costs
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=F2]{Model: a second-price auction for the target}
\framesubtitle{Who moves, who knows what, and when}
\hypertarget{main:notation}{}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[
  box/.style={draw=black!55, rounded corners=3pt, line width=0.6pt, align=left,
    text width=2.45cm, inner xsep=4pt, inner ysep=4pt},
  num/.style={circle, fill=black!65, text=white, font=\scriptsize\bfseries,
    inner sep=0pt, minimum size=11pt},
  arr/.style={-{Stealth[length=5pt]}, line width=0.7pt, black!60}]
  \node[box] (s) {\ModelBox{Seller}{announces the sale rule before any trade}};
  \node[box, right=0.33cm of s] (i) {\ModelBox{Order slot}{one unit order reaches the market}};
  \node[box, right=0.33cm of i] (m) {\ModelBox{Market makers}{see the order only; set the stock price}};
  \node[box, right=0.33cm of m, draw=cCost, line width=1.1pt] (c)
    {\ModelBox{Challenger}{sees the price and its own cost; enters or stays out}};
  \node[box, right=0.33cm of c] (b) {\ModelBox{Bidders}{the incumbent and an entered challenger bid values}};
  \foreach \x/\n in {s/1, i/2, m/3, c/4, b/5} {\node[num] at ([xshift=2pt,yshift=-1pt]\x.north west) {\n};}
  \draw[arr] (s) -- (i); \draw[arr] (i) -- (m); \draw[arr] (m) -- (c); \draw[arr] (c) -- (b);
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
\vspace{-2pt}
{\small
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
\item \textbf{Sale rule:} cash second-price auction with reserve $p$. The top bid wins and pays $\max\{p,\text{other bid}\}$. Each bidder bids its value
\item \textbf{Incumbent:} value $R\sim U[0,r]$. Strength $r$ is public; only the incumbent knows $R$
\item \textbf{Challenger:} class $j\in\{H,L\}$, prior $\pi$ on $H$, value from $G_j$. The benchmark uses point masses $h$ and $\ell$
\item The challenger learns its value after preparation, not before
\item \Cost{\textbf{Cost:} zero with probability $\rho$, else $c_H>0$, with no link to class}
\end{itemize}}
\NavGap
\PlaceNav{\hyperlink{app:notation}{\beamergotobutton{Notation}}}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M6. One auction, two claims
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=F3]{One auction, two claims, opposite responses}
\framesubtitle{Who wins and who pays at incumbent value $R$; benchmark order $p<\ell<r<h$}
\vspace{2pt}
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}llll@{}}
\toprule
Incumbent value & Class $H$ challenger & Class $L$ challenger & Gap in target proceeds\\
\midrule
$R\le\ell$ & wins, pays $\max\{p,R\}$ & wins, pays $\max\{p,R\}$ & $0$\\
$R>\ell$ & wins, pays $R$ & loses; incumbent pays $\ell$ & $R-\ell$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\vspace{-4pt}
{\small As incumbent strength $r$ rises:\par}
\vspace{-8pt}
\begin{align*}
\Info{\Delta_T=t_H-t_L=\mathbb{E}[(R-\ell)_+]}\ &\Info{\uparrow} && \text{\Info{target-payoff spread}}\\
g_j\ &\downarrow && \text{class $j$ auction profit before cost}\\
B_r(\mu)=g_L+\mu(g_H-g_L)\ &\downarrow && \text{gross profit at belief $\mu$}
\end{align*}
\vspace{-6pt}
\GrayLine{$t_j$ is expected target proceeds with a class $j$ entrant. Proposition 1: profit falls weakly under any first-order strengthening; the spread rises weakly for ranked classes.}
\vspace{2pt}
{\small At the benchmark, the spread moves $\reg{Delta_r0}\to\reg{Delta_r1}$ from $r_0$ to $r_1$, and profit at the prior moves $\reg{Bprior_r0}\to\reg{Bprior_r1_B}$.\par}
\Takeaway{One shift, opposite signs: the challenger keeps less, and proceeds depend more on class.}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M7. The order slot
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=F4]{The order slot: one trade before the decision}
\framesubtitle{The challenger sees the price, not the order and not the class}
\hypertarget{main:slot}{}
\begin{enumerate}\setlength{\itemsep}{5pt}
\item One public order opportunity comes first. The name for it is the \textbf{order slot}
\item With probability $\lambda$, the \textbf{informed investor} fills the slot. The investor sees class $j$ and picks $q\in\{-1,0,1\}$. A nonzero order costs $k$
\item With probability $1-\lambda$, a \textbf{liquidity trader} fills the slot. Sale, no order and buy have probabilities $\beta$, $1-2\beta$, $\beta$
\item No observer sees slot identity. The identity draw has no link to class, costs or $R$
\item Market makers see order $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ and set $P=\mathbb{E}[V_T\mid X]$, with $V_T$ as sale proceeds per share
\end{enumerate}
\vspace{-2pt}
{\small Set $b=(1-\lambda)\beta$ and $u=\lambda/b$: the informed presence mass relative to the liquidity mass in one direction. The number $1+u$ is the largest likelihood ratio of an order. The bound $0<\beta\le 1/3$ holds throughout.\par}
\TakeawayWithNav{Every order can come from either class. No price reveals the class with certainty.}
\PlaceNav{\hyperlink{app:slot}{\beamergotobutton{Equilibrium object}}}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M8. What the challenger learns from the price
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=F5]{The price tells the challenger a bounded belief}
\framesubtitle{Belief $\mu=\Pr(H\mid P)$ and the entry rule $e_r(\mu)$}
\hypertarget{main:belief}{}
\vspace{-4pt}
\[
m(\pi)=\frac{\pi}{\pi+(1-\pi)(1+u)}\ \le\ \mu\ \le\ \frac{\pi(1+u)}{\pi(1+u)+1-\pi}=M(\pi)
\qquad\text{for every investor strategy}
\]
\vspace{-8pt}
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccc@{}}
\toprule
Full orders at the benchmark prior & Sale $X=-1$ & No order $X=0$ & Buy $X=1$\\
\midrule
Belief $\mu$ & $\reg{m_half_B}$ & $\reg{prim_pi}$ & $\reg{M_half_B}$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\vspace{-4pt}
{\small
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
\item Price at belief $\mu$: $P_r(\mu)=t_0+e_r(\mu)\bigl(t_L-t_0+\Info{\Delta_T}\mu\bigr)$
\item Entry rule: $e_r(\mu)=\rho+(1-\rho)\,\mathbf{1}\{B_r(\mu)\ge c_H\}$, since the zero cost always pays
\item Entry at least $\rho$ and $\Delta_T>0$ let the challenger recover $\mu$ from $P$
\end{itemize}}
\TakeawayWithNav[0.3em]{A buy order moves belief up to $M(\pi)$. Belief stays short of one.}
\PlaceNav{\hyperlink{app:belief}{\beamergotobutton{Posterior bounds}}}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M9. The benchmark
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=F6]{Benchmark: only incumbent strength changes}
\framesubtitle{Declared inputs; units are arbitrary}
\hypertarget{main:bench}{}
\begin{center}\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.05}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llp{6.2cm}@{}}
\toprule
Input & Value & Meaning\\
\midrule
$h$, $\ell$ & $\reg{prim_h}$, $\reg{prim_ell}$ & class $H$ and class $L$ values\\
$p$ & $\reg{prim_p}$ & reserve price\\
$\pi$, $\rho$ & $\reg{prim_pi}$, $\reg{prim_rho}$ & prior on $H$; probability of zero cost\\
Costs $0$, $c_H$, $k$ & $0$, $\reg{prim_cH}$, $\reg{prim_k}$ & preparation costs; cost of a nonzero order\\
$\beta$, $\lambda$ & $\reg{beta_B}$, $\reg{lambda_B}$ & liquidity order chance; informed presence chance\\
$u$, $b$ & $\reg{u_B}$, $\reg{b_B}$ & mass ratio $u=\lambda/b$; here $1+u=e$\\
$r_0,r_1,r_2$ & $\reg{prim_r0}$, $\reg{prim_r1}$, $\reg{prim_r2}$ & weak, strong, stronger still\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\vspace{-4pt}
\GrayLine{Inputs illustrate the results. Inputs are not estimates from data.}
\TakeawayWithNav[0.5em]{Comparisons vary $r$ across $r_0$, $r_1$ and $r_2$ and hold all else fixed.}
\PlaceNav{\hyperlink{app:bench}{\beamergotobutton{Admissible region}}}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M10. Trade pays only against a strong incumbent
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=F7]{Trade pays only against a strong incumbent}
\framesubtitle{Residual gain per unit, before the order cost $k$; Lemma 3}
\vspace{2pt}
{\small
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{3pt}
\item Buy after $H$: expected share payoff less price. Sell after $L$: price less expected share payoff
\item Each correct order earns at most $\Info{\Delta_T}$ before cost, under every profile
\item Set $\kappa=\min\{m,1-M\}$. Each correct order earns at least $\rho\kappa\,\Info{\Delta_T}$ before cost
\end{itemize}}
\vspace{2pt}
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule
 & Bound check & Orders $(q_H,q_L)$\\
\midrule
Weak $r_0$ & $\Info{\Delta_T(r_0)}=\reg{Delta_r0}<k=\reg{prim_k}$ & $(0,0)$: no trade\\
Strong $r_1$ & $\rho\kappa\,\Info{\Delta_T(r_1)}-k=\reg{margin_kstrong_B}>0$ & $(1,-1)$: full orders\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\GrayLine{\Info{\textbf{Trading-cost window (H2):}} $\Delta_T(r_0)<k<\rho\kappa\,\Delta_T(r_1)$, at prior $\pi$.}
\Takeaway{The shift that cuts challenger profit switches informed trade on.}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M11. Only good news makes high-cost preparation pay
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=F8]{Only good news makes high-cost preparation pay}
\framesubtitle{Threshold belief $\tau(r)=(c_H-g_L)/(g_H-g_L)$, with $B_r(\tau)=c_H$}
\begin{center}
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth,height=0.42\textheight,keepaspectratio]{beliefs_talk.pdf}
\end{center}
\vspace{-6pt}
{\small
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
\item Zero cost always pays; cost $c_H$ pays exactly at beliefs at or past $\tau(r)$
\item Thresholds: $\tau(r_0)=\reg{tau_r0}$, $\tau(r_1)=\reg{tau_r1}$, $\tau(r_2)=\reg{tau_r2}$; top belief $M=\reg{M_half_B}$
\item At $r_1$, a purchase clears the threshold. Past $r_C$, no order clears it
\end{itemize}}
\Takeaway[0.3em]{The ceiling $r_C$ sits just below $r_2$.}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M12. Proposition 2
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=F9]{Proposition 2: a stronger incumbent can raise entry}
\framesubtitle{Weak $r_0$, strong $r_1$, stronger still $r_2$; all other inputs equal}
\hypertarget{main:prop2}{}
\begin{ResultBox}[Proposition 2, under the conditions below]
\small
\PropItem{(i)}\textbf{Weak $r_0$:} no trade, $(q_H,q_L)=(0,0)$; price flat; entry $=\rho$
\PropItem{(ii)}\textbf{Strong $r_1$:} full orders $(1,-1)$; price informative; entry $>\rho$
\PropItem{(iii)}\textbf{Stronger still $r_2$:} full orders; price informative; entry back to $\rho$\par
\end{ResultBox}
\vspace{-2pt}
{\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.1}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l@{\hspace{0.8em}}l@{}}
\Cost{\textbf{(H1) High-cost window}} & $B_{r_0}(\pi)<c_H<B_{r_1}(M)$\\
\Info{\textbf{(H2) Trading-cost window}} & $\Delta_T(r_0)<k<\rho\kappa\,\Delta_T(r_1)$, $\kappa=\min\{m,1-M\}$\\
\textbf{(H3) Ceiling at $r_2$} & $B_{r_2}(M)<c_H$\\
\end{tabular}\par}
\vspace{2pt}
{\small Ownership in part (ii) rises exactly if $[\rho+(1-\rho)(b+\lambda)]W_H(F_1)>\rho W_H(F_0)$, with $W_H(F)$ as the class $H$ win chance at reserve $p$.\par}
\vspace{2pt}
\GrayLine{The outcome is unique in each part, under all four tie-rule pairs. Each condition is a strict inequality, so small input moves keep each part.}
\TakeawayWithNav[0.3em]{\Info{wider $\Delta_T$ $\to$ trade pays $\to$ informative price $\to$ good news clears $c_H$ $\to$ entry at high cost}}
\PlaceNav{\hyperlink{app:prop2}{\beamergotobutton{Proof structure}}}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M13. The benchmark outcome
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=F10]{At the benchmark, entry rises and then returns}
\framesubtitle{Unique orders and entry at on-path prices}
\hypertarget{main:outcome}{}
{\footnotesize Entry is the probability that the challenger prepares. Ownership is the probability that a class $H$ challenger acquires the target.\par}
\vspace{3pt}
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{5.4cm}>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{2.1cm}>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{2.1cm}>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{2.1cm}@{}}
\toprule
 & weak $r_0$ & \textbf{strong $r_1$} & stronger still $r_2$\\
\midrule
Strength $r$ & $\reg{prim_r0}$ & $\reg{prim_r1}$ & $\reg{prim_r2}$\\
Gross profit at prior $B_r(\pi)$ & $\reg{Bprior_r0}$ & $\reg{Bprior_r1_B}$ & $\reg{Bprior_r2}$\\
\Info{Spread $\Delta_T$} & $\reg{Delta_r0}$ & $\reg{Delta_r1}$ & $\reg{Delta_r2}$\\
Orders $(q_H,q_L)$ & $(0,0)$ & $\boldsymbol{(1,-1)}$ & $(1,-1)$\\
Price & flat & \textbf{informative} & informative\\
Entry & $\reg{entry_r0}$ & \textbf{\reg{entry_r1_B}} & $\reg{entry_r2}$\\
Class $H$ ownership & $\reg{own_r0}$ & \textbf{\reg{own_r1_B}} & $\reg{own_r2_B}$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\vspace{-2pt}
\TakeawayWithNav[0.3em]{Rise, then return: past ceiling strength $\reg{rC_B}$, the best belief cannot cover $c_H$.}
\PlaceNav{\hyperlink{app:outcome}{\beamergotobutton{Entry formulas}}}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M14. The fixed-information control
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=F11]{Hold information fixed: entry does not rise}
\framesubtitle{Entry at $r_0$ and $r_1$ in the full model and in two controls; Proposition A.3}
\vspace{2pt}
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{6.8cm}ccc@{}}
\toprule
 & $r_0$ & $r_1$ & Direction\\
\midrule
Full model: price seen, trade re-solved & $\reg{entry_r0}$ & $\reg{entry_r1_B}$ & up\\
Same full orders at both strengths & $\reg{p4_frozen_r0_entry}$ & $\reg{p4_frozen_r1_entry}$ & does not rise\\
Price hidden from the challenger & $\reg{p4_hidden_r0_entry}$ & $\reg{p4_hidden_r1_entry}$ & flat\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\vspace{2pt}
{\small
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
\item At any fixed price experiment, a stronger incumbent cuts $B_r(\mu)$ at each belief: entry does not rise
\item Frozen full orders give the same entry up to $r_C$, then $\rho$. At $r_0$ the control is not an equilibrium
\item With the price hidden, cost $c_H$ never pays at the prior, so entry stays at $\rho$
\end{itemize}}
\Takeaway{The rise comes from a change in what the price reveals. Deterrence stays at each belief.}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M15. Coexistence
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=F12]{At intermediate strength, equilibria coexist}
\framesubtitle{Proposition 3 at fixed $\lambda$: no trade and informative trade side by side}
\hypertarget{main:coex}{}
\begin{center}
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth,height=0.42\textheight,keepaspectratio]{coexistence_talk.pdf}
\end{center}
\vspace{-6pt}
{\small
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
\item On $[\reg{rA},\reg{rN}]$, no informed trade (N) and an informative equilibrium coexist
\item On branch R the high class mixes its purchase; from $\reg{rF_B}$ it buys for certain (branch F)
\item Entry rises weakly on the branch, strictly on R, then stays flat at $\reg{entry_r1_B}$ until $r_C$
\end{itemize}}
\TakeawayWithNav[0.3em]{Coexistence spans $[r_A,r_N]$.}
\PlaceNav{\hyperlink{app:coex}{\beamergotobutton{Thresholds in detail}}}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M16. Competition creates research
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=F13]{Competition creates research}
\framesubtitle{Proposition 4: costly research sets presence $\lambda$, with a cap $\bar\lambda$}
\hypertarget{main:research}{}
{\small Research cost $\tfrac{a}{2}\lambda^2$; a success reveals the class and fills the slot. At $\reg{str_r155}$, $\reg{str_r160}$, $\reg{str_r165}$ research is $\reg{res_lambda_r155}$, $\reg{res_lambda_r160}$, $\reg{res_lambda_r165}$ and entry is $\reg{res_entry_r155}$, $\reg{res_entry_r160}$, $\reg{res_entry_r165}$.\par}
\vspace{1pt}
\begin{center}
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth,height=0.44\textheight,keepaspectratio]{research_talk.pdf}
\end{center}
\vspace{-6pt}
\GrayLine{The branch runs on $[r_R,\bar r_R)\approx[\reg{res_rR},\reg{res_rcap})$; entry rises from $\reg{res_entry_rR}$ to $\reg{res_entry_cap}$ (Corollary 3). Zero research is unique at $r_0$, coexists on the branch, and research at the cap is unique at $r_1$ and $r_2$.}
\TakeawayWithNav[0.3em]{Research rises along the branch while zero research remains an equilibrium; entry rises with it.}
\PlaceNav{\hyperlink{app:research}{\beamergotobutton{Research in detail}}}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M17. Robustness in one frame
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=F14]{The reversal survives changes to the model}
\framesubtitle{Each row keeps the slot and varies one part of the set-up}
\hypertarget{main:robust}{}
\vspace{2pt}
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5.2cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{8.6cm}@{}}
\toprule
Change & Result\\
\midrule
Preparation cost laws (A.4) & Reversal holds with atoms or none; entry at $r_1$ equals $\reg{p4_atomless_r1_entry}$ in the benchmark band case\\
Value classes, priors (A.5, A.6) & Holds for every ranked pair and prior at suitable costs; at benchmark costs the prior range is $(\reg{prior_lo_B},\reg{prior_hi_B})$; many classes need separation\\
Complementary signals (A.7) & At $B$ with pair $(\reg{sig_comp_aT},\reg{sig_comp_d})$, entry $\reg{p4_comp_b_r0_entry}\to\reg{p4_comp_b_r1_entry}$\\
Payment rule (A.9) & The spread response weakly has the sign of $1-2\omega$ for seller share $\omega$; sale terms sit in the next frame\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\vspace{-2pt}
\TakeawayWithNav[0.3em]{One slot and unit orders carry the result across cost, value and signal variants.}
\PlaceNav{\hyperlink{app:robust}{\beamergotobutton{Extensions}}\NavSep\hyperlink{app:sizes}{\beamergotobutton{Order sizes}}}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M18. Welfare and sale terms
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[t,label=F15]{Price access raises proceeds and surplus}
\framesubtitle{Proposition A.8 at $r_1$: price seen or price hidden, trade re-solved}
\hypertarget{main:welfare}{}
\vspace{4pt}
\begin{center}\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{5.6cm}ccc@{}}
\toprule
 & Price seen & Price hidden & Gain\\
\midrule
Expected target proceeds & $\reg{p2_base_r1_proceeds}$ & $\reg{p2_base_hidden_proceeds}$ & $\reg{p2_access_proceeds_gain}$\\
Surplus net of preparation costs & $\reg{p2_base_r1_surplus}$ & $\reg{p2_base_hidden_surplus}$ & $\reg{p2_access_surplus_gain}$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
{\small
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{3pt}
\item Surplus is acquisition surplus net of preparation costs; transfers net out
\item Price access adds preparation only after a purchase, at beliefs that cover $c_H$
\item Reserves (A.10): at the exclusion reserve entry is flat; strict deterrence at $\reg{rsv_deter}$ also excludes the weak incumbent
\end{itemize}}
\NavGap
\PlaceNav{\hyperlink{app:welfare}{\beamergotobutton{Sale terms in detail}}}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M19. Empirical implications
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=F16]{Empirical implications}
\framesubtitle{Public sales with a ready incumbent and a challenger free to prepare; Propositions A.11--A.14}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{6pt}
\item \textbf{Entry:} a stronger incumbent can raise preparation starts, at prices set before the start; with a hidden price, entry does not rise
\item \textbf{Spread:} purchase impact exceeds sale impact exactly when a purchase recruits. At $r_1$ the spread is $\reg{ba_r1_B}$, with entry share $\reg{ba_share_r1_B}$; above $r_C$ the entry component is zero
\item \textbf{Full orders:} the unique outcome for $r>r_S$, $r_S\approx\reg{rS_B}$. Sale impact and volume then identify the informed share
\item \textbf{Winners:} orders predict the winner even above $r_C$, where they no longer predict entry
\end{itemize}
\medskip
\GrayLine{Outcome: the start of costly preparation. A valid test uses the price before that start. Returns before a bid can also reflect an expected bid (Schwert 1996).}
\Takeaway{Incumbent strength, the early price path and the start of preparation move as a set.}
\end{frame}

% ======================================================================
% M20. Conclusion (no navigation)
% ======================================================================
\begin{frame}[label=F17]{Conclusion}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{18pt}
\item \KeyIdea{A stronger incumbent can bring the challenger in:} entry $\reg{entry_r0}\to\reg{entry_r1_B}$ at the benchmark, then back to $\reg{entry_r2}$ at $r_2$
\item \textbf{Why:} strength shifts a value gap to shareholders, trade pays in the slot, and a buy order makes high-cost preparation pay
\item \textbf{Implication:} competition in the auction can create competition for entry, via the stock price before preparation
\end{itemize}
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- A3
\begin{frame}[label=A3]{The equilibrium object in the slot model}
\hypertarget{app:slot}{}
{\small
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{3pt}
\item \textbf{Tuple:} order laws for each class, a price for each order in $\{-1,0,1\}$, beliefs at each price, the entry rule, the bids
\item \textbf{Prices:} $P(X)=\mathbb{E}[V_T\mid X]$ at each order, with entry at that price inside $V_T$
\item \textbf{Beliefs:} Bayes rule from the order laws at each price. Every order is on path, so no off-path belief enters
\item \textbf{Entry:} the zero cost always prepares; cost $c_H$ prepares exactly at prices with $B_r(\mu)\ge c_H$
\item \textbf{Investor:} the order law puts weight only on best replies at the stated price and entry rules, net of cost $k$
\item \textbf{Bids:} each bidder bids its value in the second-price auction
\item \textbf{Tie rules:} a tied investor may mix; a tied cost $c_H$ type prepares. Proposition 2 holds under each pair of tie rules
\end{itemize}}
\BackButton{main:slot}
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- A4
\begin{frame}[label=A4]{Posterior bounds hold for every strategy}
\hypertarget{app:belief}{}
\vspace{-2pt}
\[
\Pr(X{=}1\mid H)\le\lambda+b,\qquad \Pr(X{=}1\mid L)\ge b,\qquad b=(1-\lambda)\beta
\]
\vspace{-8pt}
{\small
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{3pt}
\item A buy order in class $H$ comes from the investor or from a liquidity buy. In class $L$, a liquidity buy alone gives chance at least $b$
\item For nonzero orders the bounds need no bound on $\beta$ past $\beta<1/2$. The bound $\beta\le 1/3$ covers the zero order
\item Likelihood ratios for $H$ against $L$ then stay in $[1/(1+u),\,1+u]$ at every order, for every investor strategy
\item Bayes rule turns that band into $m(\pi)\le\mu\le M(\pi)$ at every price
\item At the benchmark prior, the band is $[\reg{m_half_B},\reg{M_half_B}]$. Full orders attain both ends
\end{itemize}}
\Takeaway{Uniqueness proofs use bounds on every profile, not just on the candidate tuple.}
\BackButton{main:belief}
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- A5
\begin{frame}[label=A5]{The admissible region at the benchmark set-up}
\hypertarget{app:bench}{}
\vspace{2pt}
\begin{center}\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{5.4cm}p{4.2cm}p{3.6cm}@{}}
\toprule
Object & Admissible set & Benchmark pick\\
\midrule
Mass ratio $u$ (A.1) & $(\reg{u_lo},\reg{u_hi})$ & $\reg{u_B}$\\
Top belief $M$ at prior $\reg{prim_pi}$ & $(\reg{M_lo},\reg{M_hi})$ & $\reg{M_half_B}$\\
Liquidity chance $\beta$ & $0<\beta\le 1/3$ & $\reg{beta_B}$\\
Presence chance $\lambda$ at that $\beta$ & from $u=\lambda/((1-\lambda)\beta)$ & $\reg{lambda_B}$\\
Prior $\pi$ for Proposition 2 & $(\reg{prior_lo_B},\reg{prior_hi_B})$ & $\reg{prim_pi}$\\
Research cost $a$ (A.2) & $(\reg{res_a_lo},\reg{res_a_up})$ & $\reg{res_a}$\\
Research cap $\bar\lambda$ & $(\reg{res_cap_lo},\reg{res_cap_hi})$ & $\reg{res_cap}$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\GrayLine{Each set comes from strict conditions in the results. Small moves inside a set keep each result.}
\BackButton{main:bench}
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- A6
\begin{frame}[label=A6]{Proof structure of Proposition 2}
\hypertarget{app:prop2}{}
\setbeamertemplate{enumerate items}{\textbf{\insertenumlabel.}}
\begin{enumerate}\setlength{\itemsep}{4pt}
\item \textbf{Bounds for every profile:} posterior band $m\le\mu\le M$; gain per unit at most $\Delta_T$; entry at least $\rho$
\item \textbf{Weak $r_0$:} $\Delta_T(r_0)<k$ makes each nonzero order lose in expectation. No trade is the sole outcome; entry is $\rho$
\item \textbf{Strong $r_1$:} $k<\rho\kappa\,\Delta_T(r_1)$ makes each correct order pay under every profile; a wrong-signed order always loses. Orders are $(1,-1)$
\item \textbf{Entry at $r_1$:} a buy order gives belief $M$ with $B_{r_1}(M)>c_H$, so cost $c_H$ prepares after a buy order. Entry exceeds $\rho$
\item \textbf{Return at $r_2$:} trade still pays, but $B_{r_2}(M)<c_H$ keeps cost $c_H$ out at every price. Entry is $\rho$
\end{enumerate}
\vspace{2pt}
{\small Ownership: with $W_H(F)=\mathbb{E}_H[F(\theta)\mathbf{1}\{\theta\ge p\}]$, class $H$ ownership rises exactly if $[\rho+(1-\rho)(b+\lambda)]W_H(F_1)>\rho W_H(F_0)$.\par}
\BackButton{main:prop2}
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- A7
\begin{frame}[label=A7]{Entry and ownership at the benchmark}
\hypertarget{app:outcome}{}
\vspace{-2pt}
{\small Under full orders, class $H$ faces a buy order with chance $\lambda+b$ and class $L$ with chance $b$.\par}
\vspace{-4pt}
\[
e_H=\rho+(1-\rho)(\lambda+b),\qquad e_L=\rho+(1-\rho)b,\qquad
\text{entry}=\pi e_H+(1-\pi)e_L
\]
\vspace{-8pt}
{\small
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{3pt}
\item At $r_1$, cost $c_H$ prepares after a buy order and only after a buy order. Class entry rates are $e_H$ and $e_L$
\item At the benchmark prior, entry is $\reg{entry_r1_B}$ and class $H$ ownership is $\reg{own_r1_B}$
\item At $r_0$, no trade gives a flat price, so entry is $\reg{entry_r0}$ and ownership is $\reg{own_r0}$
\item At $r_2$, no price covers $c_H$, so entry is $\reg{entry_r2}$ and ownership is $\reg{own_r2_B}$, with full orders
\item Auction inputs: $B_r(\pi)$ equals $\reg{Bprior_r0}$, $\reg{Bprior_r1_B}$, $\reg{Bprior_r2}$ at $r_0$, $r_1$, $r_2$
\end{itemize}}
\BackButton{main:outcome}
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- A8
\begin{frame}[label=A8]{Coexistence thresholds in detail}
\hypertarget{app:coex}{}
\vspace{2pt}
\begin{center}\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule
Threshold & Value at the benchmark & Role\\
\midrule
$r_A$ & $\reg{rA}$ & first strength with an informative branch\\
$r_F$ & $\reg{rF_B}$ & first strength with a certain buy order on the branch\\
$r_N$ & $\reg{rN}$ & last strength with a no-trade equilibrium\\
$r_J$ & $\reg{rJ}$ & only the full purchase from here\\
$r_S$ & $\reg{rS_B}$ & low class sells for certain from here\\
$r_C$ & $\reg{rC_B}$ & ceiling: top belief stops short of $c_H$ past $r_C$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
{\small
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{3pt}
\item Before $r_A$, a buy order cannot pay at any mix rate, so no informative branch exists
\item On $[r_A,r_F)$, the mix rate adjusts with strength and entry rises with it
\item From $r_F$ to $r_N$, a full purchase coexists with no trade and entry on the branch is flat
\item Past $r_N$, no trade fails: a lone order pays at the flat price. Full orders are unique for $r>r_S$
\end{itemize}}
\BackButton{main:coex}
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- A9
\begin{frame}[label=A9]{Research in detail}
\hypertarget{app:research}{}
{\small
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{3pt}
\item Research picks $\lambda$ in $[0,\bar\lambda]$ before the slot, at cost $\tfrac{a}{2}\lambda^2$ (Proposition 4)
\item Benchmark research inputs: $a=\reg{res_a}$ and cap $\bar\lambda=\reg{res_cap}$
\item At $r_0$ the unique equilibrium has no research and no trade; entry is $\rho$
\item The branch is an equilibrium exactly on $[r_R,\bar r_R)\approx[\reg{res_rR},\reg{res_rcap})$; research rises from $\reg{res_lambda_rR}$ to the cap (Corollary 3)
\item At $\reg{str_r155}$, $\reg{str_r160}$ and $\reg{str_r165}$ there are exactly two equilibria: no research, and the branch (class $H$ buys after a success, class $L$ abstains)
\item Rates on the branch: $\reg{res_lambda_r155}$, $\reg{res_lambda_r160}$, $\reg{res_lambda_r165}$; entry: $\reg{res_entry_r155}$, $\reg{res_entry_r160}$, $\reg{res_entry_r165}$
\item At $r_1$ and $r_2$ research at the cap is unique, with trade in both directions; entry at $r_2$ is $\rho$
\end{itemize}}
\GrayLine{Costly research with an alternative arrival has precedent in Dow and Gorton 1997. The cost form and the cap are set-up choices.}
\BackButton{main:research}
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- A10
\begin{frame}[label=A10]{Extensions in detail}
\hypertarget{app:robust}{}
\vspace{2pt}
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{4.4cm}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{9.2cm}@{}}
\toprule
Variant & Statement in the slot set-up\\
\midrule
General values, priors (A.5) & Proposition 2 holds for every ranked pair and prior at suitable costs, under (H1)--(H3) with $m(\pi)$, $M(\pi)$\\
Many classes (A.6) & The result holds under a separation condition on class proceeds; without it one price can pool two posteriors\\
Cost laws (A.4) & The reversal holds with atoms or none; an atomless high component turns the ceiling drop into a ramp\\
Private signals (A.7) & At $B$, pair $(\reg{sig_comp_aT},\reg{sig_comp_d})$ gives entry $\reg{p4_comp_b_r0_entry}\to\reg{p4_comp_b_r1_entry}$; without the challenger signal entry is $\reg{p4_comp_b_no_y_r1_entry}$ at both strengths\\
Price access (A.8) & Shareholders gain in total at every trade scale below $\reg{p2_access_break_even}$\\
Payment rule (A.9) & The spread response weakly has the sign of $1-2\omega$; strictly when $\omega\ne1/2$ and $\mathbb{E}[(R-\ell)_+]$ changes strictly\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\BackButton{main:robust}
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- A11
\begin{frame}[label=A11]{Continuous order sizes need a convention}
\hypertarget{app:sizes}{}
{\small
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{4pt}
\item The slot set-up uses unit orders $\{-1,0,1\}$, so every order is on path and no off-path belief enters
\item A menu of continuous order sizes needs a convention for the sizes that no class uses, as in Edmans, Goldstein and Jiang 2015
\item Another route keeps every size on path through additive liquidity flow
\item With Laplace noise of scale $s$ and full unit orders, the top posterior equals the slot value $M(\pi)$ when $1+u=e^{2/s}$
\item The two set-ups then share the posterior bounds. They differ in the probability that each class reaches the top posterior
\end{itemize}}
\Takeaway{Unit orders keep prices on path at every order.}
\BackButton{main:robust}
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- A12
\begin{frame}[label=A12]{Sale terms in detail}
\hypertarget{app:welfare}{}
{\small
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{4pt}
\item \textbf{Price access (A.8):} at $r_1$, proceeds gain equals $\reg{p2_access_proceeds_gain}$ and net surplus gain equals $\reg{p2_access_surplus_gain}$
\item Orders and trade costs match in the two access cases at $r_1$; access adds preparation after a purchase only
\item \textbf{Reserve (A.10):} at exclusion reserve $\reg{rsv_points_excl}$, full orders hold at both strengths and entry is flat
\item Strict deterrence needs reserve $\reg{rsv_deter}$, a level that excludes the low class and the weak incumbent
\item \textbf{Payment rule (A.9):} with seller share $\omega$, the spread response weakly has the sign of $1-2\omega$; strictly when $\omega\ne1/2$ and $\mathbb{E}[(R-\ell)_+]$ changes strictly
\end{itemize}}
\BackButton{main:welfare}
\end{frame}
